verdicts.evidence: Official project generator and readiness/cleanup utilities; package SHA-256 equals the exact registry release. Neither its own code nor reviewed direct dependencies shows the credential-harvesting install payload from the historical Nx compromise.
execution_paths: index.js exports application/library/init generators; loading does not install an extra lifecycle script. Generator calls update the Nx virtual project tree, add framework/bundler dependencies and return install tasks. Application options drive Docker/Jest/ESLint/project configuration.

src/utils/wait-for-port-open.js creates net.Socket, connects to caller host/port (default localhost), retries allowed connection errors with setTimeout, then closes/unrefs the socket. This is readiness testing.

src/utils/kill-port.js checks the caller port and invokes kill-port. Fetched kill-port 1.6.1 traces to netstat/TaskKill on Windows and lsof/awk/xargs kill on Unix; process termination is real and retained as a notable capability.

CLI test templates execute the generated node entry; server templates perform local readiness checks and port cleanup. No credential search, inventory upload, encoded install payload or shell-profile modification was found.
verdicts.likely_external_label_reason: Likely package/version reputation conflation: maintainer advisory GHSA-cxm3-wv7p-598c lists @nx/node 20.9.0 and 21.5.0, not 22.6.0. The supplied source gives no exact rationale for this artifact.

classifier.disagreement: No calibrated verdict disagreement. Raw probability remains elevated, particularly for Nx; it is not treated as a behavioral verdict. Scanner warns that feature-spec v18 is older than expected v21.

verdicts.material_attack_coverage_loss: None found; all sample hostile/suspicious counts remain zero and six preexisting attack assertions retain severity. Notable false capabilities were removed, and genuine capabilities retained or relocated.

verdicts.evidence: Behavior matches documented workflow visualization and caller-configured notifications. The package matches its registry tarball; minification, embedded browser scripts, network posts and storage are explained by those code paths, with no hostile acquisition or secret-to-attacker transfer.
execution_paths: Workflow events build an in-memory IR, parallel/decision trees and timing snapshots. Renderers produce ASCII, Mermaid, flowcharts and HTML. Pako DEFLATE plus Base64URL encodes diagram source for Kroki/mermaid.ink URLs; this is representation encoding, not concealed executable staging.

kroki/fetch consumes rendered SVG text or PNG/PDF bytes and returns them to the caller. It does not evaluate downloaded code. Generated HTML can load the documented Mermaid CDN script and Google fonts.

Slack adapter receives token/channel explicitly and calls chat.postMessage/chat.update. Discord validates a caller webhook and POSTs/PATCHes diagram/status JSON. Generic webhook adapter POSTs caller workflow IR and metadata to a supplied URL. No credential-store reads or unsolicited fixed recipient was found.

Browser UI uses sessionStorage for workflow IR and localStorage for settings. Optional WebSocket URL supports snapshot seeking and heatmap controls; event values are ordinary UI input. devEvents batches opt-in workflow events to a caller URL, default localhost:4747/events.
verdicts.likely_external_label_reason: Source rationale was not supplied. A heuristic or package-level mislabel is plausible: minified browser scripts, source maps, WebClient, webhook POSTs, storage and event-value access resemble primitives also used by stealers. This is an inference; no malicious behavior was found in those paths.

verdicts.evidence: Authentic 1.61.1 SDK with local signing and caller-configured transaction/RPC traffic; no injected private-key export path found. The supplied OSV advisory affects >=1.95.6,<1.95.8, not this version.
execution_paths: src/keypair.ts creates or imports caller-provided Ed25519 key material, derives public keys and validates their relation. src/utils/ed25519.ts signs locally with ed25519.sync.sign(message, secretKey.slice(0,32)); secp256k1 helper uses signSync.

Connection.sendTransaction signs locally and passes transaction.serialize() to sendRawTransaction. transaction/legacy.ts _serialize writes signature count, signatures and serialized public message. The RPC body does not contain the signer secret key.

createRpcClient POSTs JSON-RPC requests to the caller endpoint through fetch/custom middleware, with finite HTTP-429 retries. WebSockets subscribe to blockchain events. cluster defaults point to Solana RPC services.

Source and generated IIFE/ESM/CJS variants agree. _compile() here compiles a transaction message with no source/filename arguments. Buffer.from(slice) constructs public keys/blockhash/schema buffers. cp -= 0x10000 is Unicode conversion. None establishes Node module execution, hostname collection or a shell copy command.
verdicts.likely_external_label_reason: Version-range overmatch is strongly supported: OSV currently identifies >=1.95.6,<1.95.8, while the imported historical origin initially said introduced=0. This supplied release is 1.61.1 and exactly matches npm.

analysis_method: Static execution-path review of original JS/TS, bundled variants, generated browser scripts and recovered source-map sources; no sample code executed. Atomscan local slow scans use --follow=none and this working tree. URLs/dependencies were separately fetched with forager and retained with provenance in scratch/bad-triage.

regression.result: Passed 18 capability cases and 5 existing controls

changes.correction: Split native/managed bare type recognition from opaque-data recognition. Data now needs a qualified .NET type or an extracted standalone WebClient token. Preserve the canonical consumer union; Slack source-map class names no longer claim .NET networking. C#/PowerShell download attack controls retain their prior findings.

Consolidate the sliced variant into hostname-derived buffer provenance. The old sliced rule selected any slice result and merely allowed hostname as a transfer model, so public-key byte slices falsely matched. Require hostname as the actual source and permit slice/substring as receiver-preserving transfers; update all three exact consumers.

Require a second call argument for the source/filename compiler API. Zero-argument transaction._compile() is not Node source loading. Positive Module._compile(source, filename) remains covered; encoded _compile and computed-Module atoms are unchanged.
Reject matched cp assignment operators. Unicode code-point subtraction cp -= 0x10000 is not a shell copy; real cp commands still match.

Move the neutral authorization operation out of HTTP request-action inference and require an actual parsed call. A check-role string in decision-tracking documentation proves no permission check. Update exact consumers; real check_permission calls retain notable coverage.

Do not cross a semicolon from JSON.stringify into another statement to infer that an event value was sent. Preserve the real inline JSON event-value send shape. Rename the independent read+send composite to browser-value-read-and-socket-send and describe co-occurrence; all consumers keep the same required evidence.
Relocate the Noble hashes identity fingerprint out of OTPAuth without changing matcher, scope or severity. Update the OTPAuth dependency composite.
Add conventional JavaScript deflate/deflateRaw invocation coverage, including minified pako receivers. Encoding and compression remain notable.
Extend Ed25519 signing to sync and bundler-renamed namespace receivers. Add secp256k1 sign/signSync. Both describe local cryptography, not theft.

Add generateFiles helper-call coverage and a file-local Nx Devkit import+generation composite. Use the live call node because sequence-expression invocation targets are missing from the symbol projection. Description states the required co-occurrence and does not claim proven import-to-call binding.

external_analysis.dependency_findings: All 27 fetched archives were scanned and their install hooks and relevant execution paths reviewed. Nx postinstall performs guarded workspace/cloud-client setup; bigint-buffer runs node-gyp with JS fallback. No hostile or suspicious finding was emitted for these archives. This is not used alone as evidence of benign intent.
external_analysis.url_findings: Fetched eight public reference destinations. Returned content is renderer/documentation/product code. The Solana homepage produced a suspicious auth-enrollment-domain heuristic for its link to https://passkeys.foundation/; this is a public passkey service link, not a credential-harvesting flow. That external-page heuristic is outside the original three archive findings and was not used to label the SDK malicious.
external_analysis.provenance: Original fetched bytes and .forage.json sidecars are retained in scratch/bad-triage/reference, dependencies and url-references.

limits: No machine deployment context or installed lockfile was supplied; broad dependency ranges do not identify the historical installed resolution. Reviewed dependency versions are explicitly recorded, not asserted to be a complete transitive runtime environment.

The binaries are source npm archives; analysis was static, and network requests were made only by research fetchers, without running sample entry points. Runtime reachability/success was not invented.
Cleave reports conservative flow-analysis limitations in some bundles/templates; byte-level/source review complements those projections.

A hostname-shaped public URL is not proof of credential theft. The external Solana homepage auth-domain heuristic remains a separately documented rule-taxonomy issue, not a disagreement on the three sample verdicts.
